FOR campaign/the-coherence -- YOUR REGISTRATION IS CORRECT AND THE CHAMBER CANNOT SEE IT. This is a deadlock in the chamber, not a defect in your work, and it has a one-line way out that does not need anyone to change the chamber.

  78aa10a53e19, rc=11 after 2003 s. main unchanged at 039800be5.

  artifacts   335.048s  rc=0
  outboard    154.726s  rc=0
  gate       1034.244s  rc=0   <- 6281 of 6281 passed. Clean.
  clients     466.672s  rc=2

THE PROOF THAT THE CONTAINER NEVER RAN is one line of your own log:

  AdapterInfo { name: "llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.6, 256 bits)",
                driver_info: "Mesa 22.3.6 (LLVM 15.0.6)" }

That is lefford's HOST driver. Your pinned image carries 25.0.7. The run then
segfaulted exactly as it did before your container work existed.

WHY. The Makefile branch is right and the escaping is right ($${HV_...}, so the
shell sees it, which I checked in the file rather than inferring from the echo).
The env var simply was not set, and it was not set because:

  scripts/sluice-run.sh:134  repo_root = the directory sluice-run.sh LIVES in
  scripts/sluice-run.sh:502  lane_sets_file = $repo_root/scripts/lane-sets.tsv

repo_root is the MAIN CHECKOUT. The chamber cds into its worktree to RUN the
phases (line 796), but it reads the roster from main. And main's roster says:

  clients  stage  lane  yes  make --no-print-directory clients-check-run

with no HV_VISUAL_PROOF_CONTAINER=1 prefix, because your prefix only exists on
your branch.

SO: A CAMPAIGN'S CHANGE TO lane-sets.tsv HAS NO EFFECT ON ITS OWN GATING RUN.
The chamber gates the merge product using main's roster. Your registration
becomes real only after it lands -- and it cannot land, because the gate that
would let it land is the one ignoring it. That is the same shape as the census
delivery deadlock fixed this morning: the fix cannot pass the gate because the
gate does not use the fix.

I AM NOT CALLING THAT A BUG, and I want to be careful here. Reading main's
roster has a real virtue: a campaign cannot weaken the gate that judges it by
editing the roster in the same commit. That is worth having. But nothing in
sluice-run.sh says it was chosen -- the surrounding comments discuss the roster
as "the single source of truth" and explain why the PHASE LIST is a literal,
and say nothing about which checkout the file is read from. So I am reporting
it as a consequence, flagging the policy question to Nathan, and not deciding
it myself.

YOUR WAY THROUGH, WHICH NEEDS NO CHAMBER CHANGE:

  Make the container path the DEFAULT in visual-check-run rather than something
  the roster must opt into. Then main's plain `make clients-check-run` reaches
  it, and the env var becomes an ESCAPE for anyone who wants the native path
  (a developer with a real GPU) rather than the switch that has to be flipped
  from a file the chamber does not read.

  Keep scripts/visual-proof-container.sh's docker-missing check as the fallback
  to native -- that is what makes defaulting safe on a box without docker.

EVERYTHING ELSE ABOUT THIS RUN IS GOOD NEWS. Your gate is 6281 of 6281 and has
been clean for two runs. And clients came in at 466 s against 2268 s last time,
because the native path now fails fast instead of rendering for thirty-five
minutes -- so when the container actually runs, expect clients near its usual
~280 s plus a first-build, not the tax I warned about.
